tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.en: A tangent graph climbs forever between its asymptotes — it has no highest point and no lowest point, so it has no amplitude at all.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.af: 'n Tan-grafiek klim eindeloos tussen sy asimptote: dit het geen hoogste punt en geen laagste punt nie, dus het dit glad geen amplitude nie.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.en: WATCH OUT: a negative a flips the graph upside down, but the amplitude stays POSITIVE. Amplitude is a distance — how far the graph swings away from its midline — and a distance is never negative. Write the size of a, not a with its sign.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.af: PAS OP: 'n negatiewe a draai die grafiek onderstebo, maar die amplitude bly POSITIEF. Amplitude is 'n afstand, hoe ver die grafiek van sy middelste lyn af wegswaai, en 'n afstand is nooit negatief nie. Skryf die grootte van a, nie a met sy teken nie.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.en: REMEMBER: a number inside the bracket with the x only slides the graph left or right. Sliding a graph sideways changes none of these three answers — same period, same amplitude, same range. Only b changes the period, only a changes the amplitude, and only a and q change the range.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.af: ONTHOU: 'n getal binne die hakie by die x skuif die grafiek net links of regs. 'n Skuif links of regs verander nie een van hierdie drie antwoorde nie: dieselfde periode, dieselfde amplitude, dieselfde waardeversameling. Net b verander die periode, net a verander die amplitude, en net a en q verander die waardeversameling.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#5.en: Three separate questions in one. The 4 sits with the x, so it belongs to the period. Nothing is in front of the sin and nothing is added on the end — so what does that make the amplitude, and where is the midline?
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#5.af: Drie aparte vrae in een. Die 4 staan by die x, dus behoort dit aan die periode. Niks staan voor die sin nie en niks word aan die einde bygetel nie: wat is die amplitude dan, en waar is die middelste lyn?

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.en: Range: the midline is y = 0, so go one amplitude up and one amplitude down from there.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.af: Waardeversameling: die middelste lyn is y = 0, dus gaan van daar af een amplitude op en een amplitude af.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.en: These three words describe three completely different things about the same wave, so it helps to say what each one means before you hunt for it. The period is how wide one whole wave is before the picture starts repeating — a plain sine takes 360°, and the 4 squashes four whole waves into that same space, so each one is only 90° wide. The amplitude is how far the wave swings away from its middle line, up or down. There is no number in front of the sin, so that swing is just 1. The range is the list of heights the graph actually reaches. The middle is at zero and the swing is 1, so the graph lives between −1 and 1 and never leaves. Notice that the 4 changed the period and left the other two alone — each letter has its own job.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.af: Hierdie drie woorde beskryf drie heel verskillende dinge van dieselfde golf, so dit help om te sê wat elkeen beteken voordat jy daarna soek. Die periode is hoe wyd een hele golf is voordat die prent begin herhaal: 'n gewone sin-grafiek neem 360°, en die 4 druk vier hele golwe in daardie selfde ruimte saam, dus is elkeen net 90° wyd. Die amplitude is hoe ver die golf van sy middelste lyn af wegswaai, op of af. Daar is geen getal voor die sin nie, dus is daardie swaai net 1. Die waardeversameling is die lys hoogtes wat die grafiek werklik bereik. Die middel is by nul en die swaai is 1, dus bly die grafiek tussen −1 en 1 en gaan nooit daar uit nie. Let op dat die 4 die periode verander het en die ander twee uitgelos het: elke letter het sy eie taak.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.en: The − 3 is on the end, outside everything, so it does not touch the x at all. Ask yourself what it DOES move, and then build the range from the new middle line.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.af: Die − 3 staan aan die einde, buite alles, dus raak dit glad nie aan die x nie. Vra jouself wat dit WEL skuif, en bou dan die waardeversameling vanaf die nuwe middelste lyn.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.en: Range: the − 3 drags the whole graph down, so the midline is y = −3. One amplitude each way gives −3 − 1 = −4 and −3 + 1 = −2.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.af: Waardeversameling: die − 3 skuif die hele grafiek af, dus is die middelste lyn y = −3. Een amplitude na elke kant gee −3 − 1 = −4 en −3 + 1 = −2.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.en: A number added or subtracted on the end lifts or drops the whole picture without changing its shape. Think of the graph as a wave painted on a sheet of glass: sliding the glass down by 3 does not make the wave wider and does not make it swing further, it just puts the whole thing lower. So the period stays 360° and the amplitude stays 1, and the only thing that moves is the middle line, from y = 0 down to y = −3. Build the range from that new middle: one amplitude up is −2, one amplitude down is −4. The most common slip is to write the range as [−1 ; 1] − 3 in your head and then subtract only once. Write the midline down first, then step up and down from it.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.af: 'n Getal wat aan die einde bygetel of afgetrek word, skuif die hele prent op of af sonder om sy vorm te verander. Dink aan die grafiek as 'n golf wat op 'n glasplaat geverf is: as jy die glas 3 af skuif, word die golf nie wyer nie en swaai dit nie verder nie, dit sit net die hele ding laer. Dus bly die periode 360° en die amplitude 1, en die enigste ding wat skuif, is die middelste lyn, van y = 0 af na y = −3. Bou die waardeversameling vanaf daardie nuwe middel: een amplitude op is −2, een amplitude af is −4. Die algemeenste fout is om die waardeversameling in jou kop as [−1 ; 1] − 3 te skryf en dan net een keer af te trek. Skryf eers die middelste lyn neer, en stap dan daarvandaan op en af.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.en: ${ASK}  y = tan 2x.  (A tangent graph has no amplitude — say why.)
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.af: ${ASK}  y = tan 2x.  ('n Tan-grafiek het geen amplitude nie: sê hoekom.)

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.en: A tangent graph is not a wave between a top and a bottom, so start by asking yourself what it does instead. And its plain period is not 360° — a tangent repeats itself in half that.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.af: 'n Tan-grafiek is nie 'n golf tussen 'n top en 'n bodem nie, so vra jouself eers wat dit eerder doen. En sy gewone periode is nie 360° nie: 'n tan-grafiek herhaal homself in die helfte daarvan.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.en: Period = 180° ÷ 2 = 90°   (a tangent's plain period is 180°, not 360°)
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.af: Periode = 180° ÷ 2 = 90°   ('n tan-grafiek se gewone periode is 180°, nie 360° nie)

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.en: Period = 90°  ·  Amplitude: none  ·  Range: y ∈ ℝ
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.af: Periode = 90°  ·  Amplitude: geen  ·  Waardeversameling: y ∈ ℝ

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.en: The tangent graph is the odd one out of the three and it is worth knowing exactly how. A sine or cosine is trapped between a highest point and a lowest point, and the amplitude measures that trap. A tangent has no trap: between one asymptote and the next it comes up from very far below and shoots off very far above, so there is no maximum and no minimum to measure. That is why the honest answer is not zero and not one — it is that a tangent has no amplitude, and the range is every real number. The period is the other difference: a tangent has already repeated itself after 180°, so you divide 180° by b instead of 360°. Here that gives 90°.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.af: Die tan-grafiek is die uitsondering van die drie, en dit is die moeite werd om presies te weet hoe. 'n Sin- of cos-grafiek is vasgevang tussen 'n hoogste punt en 'n laagste punt, en die amplitude meet daardie hok. 'n Tan-grafiek het geen hok nie: tussen een asimptoot en die volgende kom dit van baie ver onder af op en skiet baie ver bo uit, dus is daar geen maksimum en geen minimum om te meet nie. Daarom is die eerlike antwoord nie nul nie en ook nie een nie: 'n tan-grafiek het geen amplitude nie, en die waardeversameling is elke reële getal. Die periode is die ander verskil: 'n tan-grafiek het homself reeds ná 180° herhaal, dus deel jy 180° deur b in plaas van 360°. Hier gee dit 90°.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.en: Only one thing has changed, and it is sitting in FRONT of the sin. Decide which of the three answers that number belongs to, then write the other two down without doing any work.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.af: Net een ding het verander, en dit staan VOOR die sin. Besluit aan watter van die drie antwoorde daardie getal behoort, en skryf dan die ander twee neer sonder om enige werk te doen.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.en: Range: the midline is still y = 0, so go 3 up and 3 down.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.af: Waardeversameling: die middelste lyn is steeds y = 0, dus gaan 3 op en 3 af.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.en: The number in front stretches the wave taller without making it wider. Picture the plain sine graph drawn on a rubber sheet and then pulled straight upwards: every height gets multiplied by 3, so the peak that was at 1 is now at 3 and the trough that was at −1 is now at −3. Sideways, nothing at all has happened, so one whole wave still takes 360°. That is the useful habit here — before you calculate anything, ask which direction each number pulls. A number in front pulls vertically, a number with the x pulls horizontally, and a number on the end slides the whole thing up or down. Once you can name the direction, two of the three answers usually need no working at all.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.af: Die getal voor rek die golf hoër sonder om dit wyer te maak. Stel jou die gewone sin-grafiek voor, geteken op 'n rubbervel en dan reguit opwaarts gerek: elke hoogte word met 3 vermenigvuldig, dus is die hoogste punt wat by 1 was nou by 3, en die laagste punt wat by −1 was, is nou by −3. Horisontaal het glad niks gebeur nie, dus neem een hele golf steeds 360°. Dit is die nuttige gewoonte hier: voordat jy enigiets bereken, vra in watter rigting elke getal trek. 'n Getal voor trek vertikaal, 'n getal by die x trek horisontaal, en 'n getal aan die einde skuif die hele ding op of af. Sodra jy die rigting kan noem, het twee van die drie antwoorde gewoonlik glad geen werk nodig nie.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.en: The 120° is inside the bracket, joined to the x, so it moves the graph sideways. Now ask the important question: does moving a graph sideways change how wide one wave is, how far it swings, or which heights it reaches?
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#2.af: Die 120° is binne die hakie, saam met die x, dus skuif dit die grafiek links of regs. Vra nou die belangrike vraag: verander 'n skuif links of regs hoe wyd een golf is, hoe ver dit swaai, of watter hoogtes dit bereik?

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.en: Period = 360° ÷ 1 = 360°   (the 120° slides the graph, it does not squash it)
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.af: Periode = 360° ÷ 1 = 360°   (die 120° skuif die grafiek, dit druk dit nie saam nie)

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.en: Range: the midline is still y = 0, so one up and one down.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.af: Waardeversameling: die middelste lyn is steeds y = 0, dus een op en een af.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.en: This one is a trap dressed up as work. A number added to the x inside the bracket shifts the whole graph left or right, and a sideways shift is the one move that changes none of these three answers. The wave is still exactly as wide as it was, it still swings exactly as far, and it still reaches exactly the same heights — it just arrives at them earlier. So all three answers are the plain-cosine answers. Learners lose marks here by feeling that a question with a number in it must need a calculation, and then dividing 360° by 120° or adding 120° to something. Read where the number lives first. Inside the bracket next to the x, on its own, means slide, and slide means nothing changes.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.af: Hierdie een is 'n strik wat soos werk lyk. 'n Getal wat binne die hakie by die x getel word, skuif die hele grafiek links of regs, en 'n skuif links of regs is die een beweging wat nie een van hierdie drie antwoorde verander nie. Die golf is steeds presies so wyd soos voorheen, dit swaai steeds presies so ver, en dit bereik steeds presies dieselfde hoogtes: dit kom net vroeër daar aan. Dus is al drie antwoorde dieselfde as vir die gewone cos-grafiek. Leerders verloor hier punte omdat hulle voel 'n vraag met 'n getal in moet 'n berekening nodig hê, en dan deel hulle 360° deur 120° of tel 120° by iets. Lees eers waar die getal woon. Binne die hakie langs die x, op sy eie, beteken skuif, en skuif beteken niks verander nie.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.en: Two things to notice. It is a tangent, so its plain period is not 360°. And the + 4 lifts the whole graph — but think carefully about whether lifting a graph that already reaches every height changes the range.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.af: Let op twee dinge. Dit is 'n tan-grafiek, dus is sy gewone periode nie 360° nie. En die + 4 skuif die hele grafiek op, maar dink mooi: verander die waardeversameling as jy 'n grafiek wat reeds elke hoogte bereik, opskuif?

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.en: Period = 180°  ·  Amplitude: none  ·  Range: y ∈ ℝ
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.af: Periode = 180°  ·  Amplitude: geen  ·  Waardeversameling: y ∈ ℝ

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.en: Lifting a tangent graph by 4 does move it — every point on the picture goes up by 4, and the place where it crosses the y-axis moves from 0 to 4. But the range does not change, and that surprises people. The reason is that a tangent already reaches every single real height before you lift it. Push all those heights up by 4 and you still have every real height, just handed out at different x-values. So the range is still y ∈ ℝ. The period is untouched too, because + 4 is outside and never touches the x. The one thing you should be able to say out loud: it still has no amplitude, because it still has no highest or lowest point to measure between.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#3.af: As jy 'n tan-grafiek 4 opskuif, skuif dit wel: elke punt op die prent gaan 4 op, en die plek waar dit die y-as sny, skuif van 0 na 4. Maar die waardeversameling verander nie, en dit verras mense. Die rede is dat 'n tan-grafiek reeds elke enkele reële hoogte bereik voordat jy dit opskuif. Druk al daardie hoogtes 4 op en jy het steeds elke reële hoogte, net by ander x-waardes uitgedeel. Dus is die waardeversameling steeds y ∈ ℝ. Die periode bly ook onaangeraak, want + 4 staan buite en raak nooit aan die x nie. Die een ding wat jy hardop moet kan sê: dit het steeds geen amplitude nie, want dit het steeds geen hoogste of laagste punt om tussen te meet nie.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#4.en: Amplitude is a distance, and a distance is never negative. Work out how far the graph swings from its midline, and let the minus sign do its own separate job.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#4.af: Amplitude is 'n afstand, en 'n afstand is nooit negatief nie. Werk uit hoe ver die grafiek van sy middelste lyn af swaai, en laat die minusteken sy eie aparte taak doen.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#4.en: Range: the midline is y = 0 and the swing is 2, so the graph runs from −2 up to 2. The minus only turns the picture upside down; it does not change WHICH heights are reached.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#4.af: Waardeversameling: die middelste lyn is y = 0 en die swaai is 2, dus loop die grafiek van −2 tot by 2. Die minus draai net die prent onderstebo; dit verander nie WATTER hoogtes bereik word nie.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#4.en: The minus sign has exactly one job: it turns the graph upside down in the x-axis. A plain cosine starts at the top on the y-axis, so −2 cos x starts at the bottom instead. What the minus does NOT do is make the amplitude negative, because amplitude means how far the graph swings away from the middle, and a how-far is always a positive number. Write it as |a| every single time and the sign takes care of itself. The range is the other place people go wrong: because the graph is flipped, they expect a flipped range, but the same set of heights is still visited — the graph just visits them in the opposite order. Top is still 2, bottom is still −2, so the range is unchanged.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#4.af: Die minusteken het presies een taak: dit reflekteer die grafiek in die x-as. 'n Gewone cos-grafiek begin bo op die y-as, dus begin −2 cos x eerder onder. Wat die minus NIE doen nie, is om die amplitude negatief te maak, want amplitude beteken hoe ver die grafiek van die middel af wegswaai, en 'n hoe-ver is altyd 'n positiewe getal. Skryf dit elke keer as |a| en die teken sorg vir homself. Die waardeversameling is die ander plek waar mense foute maak: omdat die grafiek gereflekteer is, verwag hulle 'n omgekeerde waardeversameling, maar dieselfde hoogtes word steeds besoek, die grafiek besoek hulle net in die omgekeerde volgorde. Bo is steeds 2, onder is steeds −2, dus bly die waardeversameling dieselfde.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#4.en: Two numbers, two different jobs. One of them is in front and one of them is with the x. Sort out which is which before you write anything down.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#4.af: Twee getalle, twee verskillende take. Een staan voor en een staan by die x. Sorteer uit watter een watter is voordat jy iets neerskryf.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#4.en: Range: the midline is y = 0, so 5 up and 5 down.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#4.af: Waardeversameling: die middelste lyn is y = 0, dus 5 op en 5 af.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#5.en: When two numbers appear at once, name each one's direction before you calculate. The 5 is in front of the sin, so it works vertically — it stretches the wave to five times its height. The 3 is with the x, so it works horizontally — it squashes three whole waves into the space one used to take, which makes each wave 120° wide instead of 360°. Because the two numbers pull in different directions they never interfere with each other, and that is the good news: you can answer the period without even looking at the 5, and the amplitude without even looking at the 3. The range then comes free, because the midline has not moved: five above zero and five below.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#5.af: As twee getalle saam verskyn, noem elkeen se rigting voordat jy bereken. Die 5 staan voor die sin, dus werk dit vertikaal: dit rek die golf tot vyf keer sy hoogte. Die 3 staan by die x, dus werk dit horisontaal: dit druk drie hele golwe saam in die ruimte wat een vroeër gevat het, wat elke golf 120° wyd maak in plaas van 360°. Omdat die twee getalle in verskillende rigtings trek, steur hulle mekaar nooit nie, en dit is die goeie nuus: jy kan die periode beantwoord sonder om eers na die 5 te kyk, en die amplitude sonder om eers na die 3 te kyk. Die waardeversameling kom dan verniet, want die middelste lyn het nie geskuif nie: vyf bo nul en vyf onder.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#5.en: A fraction in front is still just an amplitude — it makes the wave shorter instead of taller. Take the size of it and leave the minus out of the amplitude.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#5.af: 'n Breuk voor is steeds net 'n amplitude: dit maak die golf laer in plaas van hoër. Neem die grootte daarvan en laat die minus uit die amplitude uit.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#5.en: Range: the midline is y = 0 and the swing is ½ each way.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#5.af: Waardeversameling: die middelste lyn is y = 0 en die swaai is ½ na elke kant.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#5.en: Period = 180°  ·  Amplitude = ½  ·  Range: y ∈ [−½ ; ½]
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#5.af: Periode = 180°  ·  Amplitude = ½  ·  Waardeversameling: y ∈ [−½ ; ½]

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#5.en: A fraction in front of the sin does the same job as a whole number, only the other way round. Multiplying every height by a half squashes the wave flat instead of stretching it tall, so the peak drops from 1 to a half and the trough rises from −1 to minus a half. The minus in front then flips that flattened wave upside down, which changes where the peaks and troughs sit along the x-axis but not how high or low they go. So the amplitude is a half and the range runs from minus a half to a half. Meanwhile the 2 is doing its own separate horizontal job, fitting two whole waves into 360° so that each one is 180° wide. Two numbers, two directions, no interference.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#5.af: 'n Breuk voor die sin doen dieselfde taak as 'n heelgetal, net andersom. As jy elke hoogte met 'n half vermenigvuldig, druk dit die golf plat in plaas van om dit hoog te rek, dus sak die hoogste punt van 1 na 'n half en die laagste punt styg van −1 na minus 'n half. Die minus voor draai daardie plat golf dan onderstebo, wat verander waar die hoogste en laagste punte langs die x-as lê, maar nie hoe hoog of laag hulle gaan nie. Dus is die amplitude 'n half en loop die waardeversameling van minus 'n half tot 'n half. Intussen doen die 2 sy eie aparte horisontale taak: dit pas twee hele golwe in 360°, sodat elkeen 180° wyd is. Twee getalle, twee rigtings, geen steuring nie.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#6.en: Find the midline first — it is the number on the end. Then step one amplitude up from it and one amplitude down from it, and you have the range without guessing.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#6.af: Vind eers die middelste lyn: dit is die getal aan die einde. Stap dan een amplitude op en een amplitude af daarvandaan, en jy het die waardeversameling sonder om te raai.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#6.en: Range: the + 2 lifts the midline to y = 2. One amplitude up is 2 + 3 = 5; one amplitude down is 2 − 3 = −1.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#6.af: Waardeversameling: die + 2 lig die middelste lyn na y = 2. Een amplitude op is 2 + 3 = 5; een amplitude af is 2 − 3 = −1.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#6.en: This is the shape most range mistakes happen on, so it is worth a fixed routine: write the midline, then step. The midline is the number on the end, here y = 2 — that is the line the wave rocks about. The amplitude is how far it rocks, here 3. So the top of the wave is 2 + 3 = 5 and the bottom is 2 − 3 = −1, and the range is everything in between. Two slips to avoid. The first is writing the range as [−3 ; 3] and forgetting the lift altogether. The second is adding the 2 to only one end, which gives an answer that is not the right width. If you check nothing else, check that the distance between your two range numbers is twice the amplitude — here 5 − (−1) = 6, which is 2 × 3.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#6.af: Op hierdie vorm gebeur die meeste foute met die waardeversameling, dus is 'n vaste roetine die moeite werd: skryf die middelste lyn, en stap dan. Die middelste lyn is die getal aan die einde, hier y = 2: dit is die lyn waaroor die golf wieg. Die amplitude is hoe ver dit wieg, hier 3. Dus is die top van die golf 2 + 3 = 5 en die bodem 2 − 3 = −1, en die waardeversameling is alles tussenin. Twee foute om te vermy. Die eerste is om die waardeversameling as [−3 ; 3] te skryf en die skuif op heeltemal te vergeet. Die tweede is om die 2 by net een kant te tel, wat 'n antwoord gee wat nie die regte wydte het nie. As jy niks anders kontroleer nie, kontroleer dat die afstand tussen die twee getalle van jou waardeversameling twee keer die amplitude is: hier 5 − (−1) = 6, en dit is 2 × 3.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#6.en: Dividing by a half is the same as multiplying by 2 — so this graph is going to be wider than a plain cosine, not narrower. Do that division carefully and remember the amplitude is a size.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#6.af: Om deur 'n half te deel, is dieselfde as om met 2 te vermenigvuldig: dus gaan hierdie grafiek wyer as 'n gewone cos-grafiek wees, nie nouer nie. Doen daardie deling versigtig en onthou die amplitude is 'n grootte.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#6.en: Range: the midline is y = 0 and the swing is 2 each way.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#6.af: Waardeversameling: die middelste lyn is y = 0 en die swaai is 2 na elke kant.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#6.en: A b smaller than 1 stretches the graph sideways instead of squashing it, and the arithmetic is the part to slow down on. Dividing by a half means asking how many halves fit into 360°, and the answer is 720 — twice as many, not half as many. So this cosine takes 720° to complete one single wave, which means on an ordinary 0° to 360° set of axes you would only see half of one wave. That is a genuinely useful thing to be able to picture. The minus in front does its usual flip, so instead of starting at its highest point on the y-axis this graph starts at its lowest, but the amplitude is still the positive number 2 and the heights it reaches are still everything from −2 to 2.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#6.af: 'n b kleiner as 1 rek die grafiek horisontaal in plaas van om dit saam te druk, en die rekenwerk is die deel waar jy stadiger moet gaan. Om deur 'n half te deel, beteken om te vra hoeveel helftes in 360° pas, en die antwoord is 720: twee keer soveel, nie die helfte nie. Dus neem hierdie cos-grafiek 720° om een enkele golf te voltooi, wat beteken dat jy op gewone asse van 0° tot 360° net die helfte van een golf sal sien. Dit is regtig nuttig om dit te kan voorstel. Die minus voor doen sy gewone refleksie, dus begin hierdie grafiek op die y-as by sy laagste punt in plaas van by sy hoogste, maar die amplitude is steeds die positiewe getal 2 en die hoogtes wat dit bereik, is steeds alles van −2 tot 2.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#7.en: The minus flips it, and the 3 squashes it. Only one of those two changes an answer here — and remember which number a tangent's period starts from.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#7.af: Die minus draai dit onderstebo, en die 3 druk dit saam. Net een van die twee verander hier 'n antwoord, en onthou van watter getal 'n tan-grafiek se periode begin.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#7.en: Period = 60°  ·  Amplitude: none  ·  Range: y ∈ ℝ
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#7.af: Periode = 60°  ·  Amplitude: geen  ·  Waardeversameling: y ∈ ℝ

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#7.en: Two numbers, and only one of them earns a mark. The 3 is with the x, so it squashes the graph sideways: a tangent already repeats every 180°, and three of them now fit into that space, so the period is 60°. The minus in front flips the picture upside down, which turns a branch that was climbing into a branch that is falling. That is a real change to the drawing, but it changes nothing you have been asked for. The amplitude is still nothing at all, because flipping a graph with no top and no bottom leaves it with no top and no bottom, and the range is still every real number, because flipping every height gives you back the same collection of heights.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#7.af: Twee getalle, en net een van hulle verdien 'n punt. Die 3 staan by die x, dus druk dit die grafiek horisontaal saam: 'n tan-grafiek herhaal reeds elke 180°, en drie daarvan pas nou in daardie ruimte, dus is die periode 60°. Die minus voor draai die prent onderstebo, wat 'n tak wat geklim het, verander in 'n tak wat daal. Dit is 'n regte verandering aan die skets, maar dit verander niks wat gevra word nie. Daar is steeds glad geen amplitude nie, want as jy 'n grafiek sonder top en bodem reflekteer, het dit steeds geen top en bodem nie, en die waardeversameling is steeds elke reële getal, want as jy elke hoogte reflekteer, kry jy dieselfde versameling hoogtes terug.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#7.en: Two things are happening at once: a flip and a lift. Only one of them touches the range. Find the midline, then step one amplitude each way from it.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#7.af: Twee dinge gebeur tegelyk: 'n refleksie en 'n skuif op. Net een van hulle raak aan die waardeversameling. Vind die middelste lyn, en stap dan een amplitude na elke kant daarvandaan.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#7.en: Range: the + 3 puts the midline at y = 3. One amplitude up is 3 + 1 = 4; one amplitude down is 3 − 1 = 2. The flip changes where the graph is high and where it is low, not how high and how low.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#7.af: Waardeversameling: die + 3 sit die middelste lyn by y = 3. Een amplitude op is 3 + 1 = 4; een amplitude af is 3 − 1 = 2. Die refleksie verander waar die grafiek hoog en waar dit laag is, nie hoe hoog en hoe laag nie.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.en: Take the two changes one at a time and neither is hard. The minus flips the sine upside down, so it dips first instead of rising first. The + 3 then lifts the whole flipped wave three units, which drags the midline from y = 0 up to y = 3. Now build the range the same way you always do: midline 3, amplitude 1, so the top is 4 and the bottom is 2. Something worth noticing here is that this graph never touches the x-axis at all — its lowest point is 2, which is still above zero. A graph that sits entirely above the x-axis has no x-intercepts, and questions love asking about that. The flip contributes nothing to any of the three answers; it only decides which way round the wave runs.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.af: Vat die twee veranderinge een op 'n slag, en nie een is moeilik nie. Die minus draai die sin-grafiek onderstebo, dus daal dit eers in plaas van om eers te styg. Die + 3 skuif dan die hele gereflekteerde golf drie eenhede op, wat die middelste lyn van y = 0 na y = 3 opskuif. Bou nou die waardeversameling soos altyd: middelste lyn 3, amplitude 1, dus is die top 4 en die bodem 2. Iets wat die moeite werd is om op te let: hierdie grafiek raak glad nooit aan die x-as nie, want sy laagste punt is 2, wat steeds bo nul is. 'n Grafiek wat heeltemal bo die x-as lê, het geen x-afsnitte nie, en vrae vra graag daaroor. Die refleksie dra niks by tot enige van die drie antwoorde nie; dit besluit net in watter rigting die golf loop.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.en: One of these two numbers changes an answer and the other one is a decoy. Decide what each one does to the picture before you write a single thing down.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.af: Een van hierdie twee getalle verander 'n antwoord en die ander een is 'n lokvoël. Besluit wat elkeen aan die prent doen voordat jy een enkele ding neerskryf.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.en: Period = 360° ÷ 1 = 360°   (b = 1; the 135° is a sideways slide, not a squash)
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.af: Periode = 360° ÷ 1 = 360°   (b = 1; die 135° skuif, dit druk nie saam nie)

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.en: Range: nothing was added on the end, so the midline is still y = 0. Two up and two down.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.af: Waardeversameling: niks is aan die einde bygetel nie, dus is die middelste lyn steeds y = 0. Twee op en twee af.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.en: Everything here turns on where each number is standing. The 2 is in front, so it stretches the graph vertically and it owns the amplitude. The 135° is inside the bracket, added to the x, so it slides the graph sideways — and a sideways slide is the one transformation that leaves the period, the amplitude and the range all untouched. Learners lose this mark by treating the 135° as though it were a b and dividing 360° by it, which gives a period no cosine graph has ever had. A quick sanity check that always works: b is whatever is MULTIPLYING the x. Here nothing is multiplying the x, so b is 1 and the period is a plain 360°. The 135° only decides where the first peak lands.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.af: Alles hier hang af van waar elke getal staan. Die 2 staan voor, dus rek dit die grafiek vertikaal en dit besit die amplitude. Die 135° is binne die hakie, by die x getel, dus skuif dit die grafiek links of regs, en 'n skuif links of regs is die een transformasie wat die periode, die amplitude en die waardeversameling almal onaangeraak laat. Leerders verloor hierdie punt deur die 135° te behandel asof dit 'n b is en 360° daardeur te deel, wat 'n periode gee wat geen cos-grafiek nog ooit gehad het nie. 'n Vinnige kontrole wat altyd werk: b is wat ook al die x VERMENIGVULDIG. Hier vermenigvuldig niks die x nie, dus is b gelyk aan 1 en die periode 'n gewone 360°. Die 135° besluit net waar die eerste piek land.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.en: The half in front is tempting to call an amplitude — but ask yourself first whether this graph has a highest and a lowest point for an amplitude to measure between.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#8.af: Dit is aanloklik om die half voor 'n amplitude te noem, maar vra jouself eers of hierdie grafiek 'n hoogste en 'n laagste punt het waartussen 'n amplitude kan meet.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#9.en: Period = 45°  ·  Amplitude: none  ·  Range: y ∈ ℝ
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#9.af: Periode = 45°  ·  Amplitude: geen  ·  Waardeversameling: y ∈ ℝ

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#9.en: This is the tangent question written to catch you, and the bait is the half in front. On a sine or a cosine that half would be the amplitude, and writing a half here feels completely reasonable. But amplitude is defined as the distance from the midline to the highest point, and a tangent graph has no highest point, so there is no such distance to report — the honest answer stays no amplitude, not a half. What the half actually does is squash the branches closer to the vertical, which changes the picture but not the range: the graph still climbs to every possible height between one asymptote and the next. The 4 does the only work that earns a mark, cutting the tangent's 180° period down to 45°.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#9.af: Dit is die tan-vraag wat geskryf is om jou te vang, en die lokaas is die half voor. Op 'n sin- of cos-grafiek sou daardie half die amplitude wees, en om hier 'n half te skryf, voel heeltemal redelik. Maar amplitude is gedefinieer as die afstand van die middelste lyn tot by die hoogste punt, en 'n tan-grafiek het geen hoogste punt nie, dus is daar geen sodanige afstand om te gee nie: die eerlike antwoord bly geen amplitude nie, nie 'n half nie. Wat die half eintlik doen, is om die takke nader aan die vertikaal saam te druk, wat die prent verander maar nie die waardeversameling nie: die grafiek klim steeds tot elke moontlike hoogte tussen een asimptoot en die volgende. Die 4 doen die enigste werk wat 'n punt verdien: dit sny die tan-grafiek se periode van 180° af na 45°.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#9.en: Ask how many halves fit into 360° — that is the division you actually need. Then check your answer feels right: does a b below 1 make the graph wider or narrower?
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#9.af: Vra hoeveel helftes in 360° pas: dit is die deling wat jy eintlik nodig het. Kontroleer dan of jou antwoord reg voel: maak 'n b onder 1 die grafiek wyer of nouer?

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#9.en: Range: the midline is y = 0, so 6 up and 6 down.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#9.af: Waardeversameling: die middelste lyn is y = 0, dus 6 op en 6 af.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#9.en: The two numbers here pull as hard as they can in opposite directions, which makes this a good one to picture rather than only calculate. The 6 stretches the wave up and down until it reaches from −6 to 6, so it is a tall graph. The half stretches it sideways, doubling how long one wave takes, so it is also a very wide graph — one single wave now takes a full 720°, which is two turns of the circle. The division is the part to be careful with. Dividing by a half never makes a number smaller: 360° ÷ ½ is the same as 360° × 2, which is 720°. If your period comes out at 180° you have divided the wrong way round, and a quick picture of one long slow wave is enough to catch it.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#9.af: Die twee getalle hier trek so hard as wat hulle kan in heel verskillende rigtings, so dit is 'n goeie een om voor te stel eerder as net te bereken. Die 6 rek die golf op en af totdat dit van −6 tot 6 strek, dus is dit 'n hoë grafiek. Die half rek dit horisontaal en verdubbel hoe lank een golf neem, dus is dit ook 'n baie wye grafiek: een enkele golf neem nou 'n volle 720°, wat twee keer om die sirkel is. Die deling is die deel waarmee jy versigtig moet wees. Om deur 'n half te deel, maak 'n getal nooit kleiner nie: 360° ÷ ½ is dieselfde as 360° × 2, en dit is 720°. As jou periode 180° uitkom, het jy verkeerd om gedeel, en 'n vinnige prentjie van een lang, stadige golf is genoeg om dit te vang.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#9.en: Two minus signs, and they are doing two completely different jobs. One flips the graph and one drops it. Find the midline first, then step one amplitude each way from there.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#9.af: Twee minustekens, en hulle doen twee heel verskillende take. Een draai die grafiek onderstebo en een skuif dit af. Vind eers die middelste lyn, en stap dan een amplitude na elke kant daarvandaan.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.en: Range: the − 2 on the end puts the midline at y = −2. One amplitude up is −2 + 1 = −1; one amplitude down is −2 − 1 = −3.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.af: Waardeversameling: die − 2 aan die einde sit die middelste lyn by y = −2. Een amplitude op is −2 + 1 = −1; een amplitude af is −2 − 1 = −3.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.en: Two minus signs in one equation, and they never mean the same thing. The first one sits in front of the cos and flips the graph upside down. The second one sits on the end and drops the whole picture two units. Sort them by position, not by feel. The amplitude comes from the first: the size of −1 is 1. The midline comes from the second: y = −2. Then step, and be careful with the signs on the way — one up from −2 is −1, one down from −2 is −3, so the range is from −3 to −1. Write the smaller number first, always. This graph lives entirely below the x-axis, which is another way to check your answer: if either end of your range came out positive, something has gone wrong.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.af: Twee minustekens in een vergelyking, en hulle beteken nooit dieselfde ding nie. Die eerste een staan voor die cos en draai die grafiek onderstebo. Die tweede een staan aan die einde en skuif die hele prent twee eenhede af. Sorteer hulle volgens posisie, nie volgens gevoel nie. Die amplitude kom van die eerste: die grootte van −1 is 1. Die middelste lyn kom van die tweede: y = −2. Stap dan, en wees versigtig met die tekens op pad: een op van −2 is −1, een af van −2 is −3, dus is die waardeversameling van −3 tot −1. Skryf altyd die kleiner getal eerste. Hierdie grafiek lê heeltemal onder die x-as, wat nog 'n manier is om jou antwoord te kontroleer: as enige kant van jou waardeversameling positief uitgekom het, het iets verkeerd geloop.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.en: Two numbers, and neither of them is a b. Work out what is actually multiplying the x, and remember what a sideways slide does to a range.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.af: Twee getalle, en nie een van hulle is 'n b nie. Werk uit wat die x eintlik vermenigvuldig, en onthou wat 'n skuif links of regs aan 'n waardeversameling doen.

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.en: Period = 180° ÷ 1 = 180°   (nothing is multiplying the x, so b = 1; the 30° only slides the graph)
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.af: Periode = 180° ÷ 1 = 180°   (niks vermenigvuldig die x nie, dus b = 1; die 30° skuif net die grafiek)

tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.en: This is the hardest-looking one on the card and the shortest to answer, which is exactly why it is here. There are two numbers, and neither of them changes a single thing you have been asked for. The 3 in front would be an amplitude on a sine or cosine, but a tangent has no highest or lowest point, so there is nothing for it to measure. The 30° inside the bracket slides the whole graph 30° to the right, and a sideways slide never changes a period, an amplitude or a range. The only number that matters is the invisible 1 multiplying the x, which gives a period of 180°. If you can look at an equation and say confidently which numbers are decoys, you are reading the form properly rather than pattern-matching.
tgraph-siblings-period-amplitude-range#1.af: Hierdie een lyk die moeilikste op die kaart en is die vinnigste om te beantwoord, en dit is presies hoekom dit hier is. Daar is twee getalle, en nie een van hulle verander iets wat gevra word nie. Die 3 voor sou op 'n sin- of cos-grafiek 'n amplitude wees, maar 'n tan-grafiek het geen hoogste of laagste punt nie, dus is daar niks vir dit om te meet nie. Die 30° binne die hakie skuif die hele grafiek 30° na regs, en 'n skuif links of regs verander nooit 'n periode, 'n amplitude of 'n waardeversameling nie. Die enigste getal wat saak maak, is die onsigbare 1 wat die x vermenigvuldig, en dit gee 'n periode van 180°. As jy na 'n vergelyking kan kyk en met selfvertroue kan sê watter getalle lokvoëls is, lees jy die vorm reg in plaas van om net patrone na te boots.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en:
The sketch shows the graphs of  f(x) = 2 sin x  and  g(x) = 2 cos x  for  x ∈ [−180° ; 180°].  The graphs cut each other at A(45° ; 1,41) and at one other point.

Write down the period of f.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af:
Die skets toon die grafieke van  f(x) = 2 sin x  en  g(x) = 2 cos x  vir  x ∈ [−180° ; 180°].  Die grafieke sny mekaar by A(45° ; 1,41) en by een ander punt.

Skryf die periode van f neer.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Nothing is multiplying the x, so this is a plain sine graph as far as its width goes.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Niks vermenigvuldig die x nie, so wat sy breedte betref, is dit 'n gewone sin-grafiek.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: b = 1, so the period is  360° ÷ 1.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: b = 1, so die periode is  360° ÷ 1.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: period = 360°
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: periode = 360°

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: When a question hands you two graphs at once, the first thing to do is read each equation on its own and note what is different about it. Here f has a 2 in front, which is about height, and nothing at all with the x, which means its width is untouched. So its period is the plain 360°, and the sketch agrees: exactly one complete wave of f fits across the whole interval. The 2 in front is a decoy for this particular question, and being able to say confidently that it does not affect the period is what the mark is really for.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: As 'n vraag jou twee grafieke tegelyk gee, lees eers elke vergelyking op sy eie en let op wat anders daaraan is. Hier het f 'n 2 voor, wat oor hoogte gaan, en niks by die x nie, wat beteken sy breedte is onaangeraak. Dus is sy periode die gewone 360°, en die skets stem saam: presies een volledige golf van f pas oor die hele interval. Die 2 voor is vir hierdie vraag 'n lokval, en die punt is eintlik daarvoor dat jy met selfvertroue kan sê dit beïnvloed nie die periode nie.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Write down the amplitude of g.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Skryf die amplitude van g neer.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Careful which graph you are answering about. Amplitude is the size of the number in front of the cos.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Pas op oor watter grafiek jy antwoord. Amplitude is die grootte van die getal voor die cos.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: For  g(x) = 2 cos x,  amplitude = |a| = |2|.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Vir  g(x) = 2 cos x,  amplitude = |a| = |2|.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: amplitude = 2
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: amplitude = 2

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: The commonest way to lose this mark is to answer about the wrong graph, so check the letter in the question before you look at anything else. Here it is g, and g is the cosine. Its amplitude is the size of the number in front, which is 2, and the picture backs that up — g reaches up to 2 and down to −2. The two graphs on this sketch happen to have the same amplitude, which makes them the same height as each other; that is a coincidence of this question, not a rule, and on most exam sketches the two curves have different amplitudes on purpose.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Die algemeenste manier om hierdie punt te verloor, is om oor die verkeerde grafiek te antwoord, so kyk na die letter in die vraag voordat jy na enigiets anders kyk. Hier is dit g, en g is die cos-grafiek. Sy amplitude is die grootte van die getal voor, wat 2 is, en die prentjie bevestig dit: g gaan op tot 2 en af tot −2. Die twee grafieke op hierdie skets het toevallig dieselfde amplitude, wat hulle ewe hoog maak; dit is toeval in hierdie vraag, nie 'n reël nie, en op die meeste eksamensketse het die twee kurwes doelbewus verskillende amplitudes.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: For how many values of x in the given interval is  f(x) = g(x)?
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Vir hoeveel waardes van x in die gegewe interval is  f(x) = g(x)?

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Two graphs are equal exactly where they cut each other. Count the crossing points on the sketch — do not solve anything.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Twee grafieke is presies gelyk waar hulle mekaar sny. Tel die snypunte op die skets: moenie iets oplos nie.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: f(x) = g(x)  happens where the two curves cut each other.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: f(x) = g(x)  gebeur waar die twee kurwes mekaar sny.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: They cut twice in the interval  ∴  2 values of x
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Hulle sny twee keer in die interval  ∴  2 waardes van x

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: The whole idea behind reading a graph is that a picture answers some questions faster than algebra ever could, and this is one of them. Asking where f equals g is asking where the two curves have the same height at the same x, which is exactly where they cross. So you count crossings. The question gave you one of them, A, and the sketch shows a second down in the bottom left. There are no others inside this interval. Get into the habit of tracing across the whole interval with a finger rather than glancing — a crossing hiding near the edge of the picture is easy to miss, and it changes the answer.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Die hele idee agter grafieklees is dat 'n prentjie sommige vrae vinniger beantwoord as wat algebra ooit kan, en dit is een daarvan. Om te vra waar f gelyk is aan g, is om te vra waar die twee kurwes by dieselfde x dieselfde hoogte het, en dit is presies waar hulle mekaar sny. Dus tel jy snypunte. Die vraag het jou een gegee, A, en die skets wys 'n tweede links onder. Daar is geen ander binne hierdie interval nie. Kry die gewoonte om met 'n vinger oor die hele interval te volg eerder as om net vinnig te kyk: 'n snypunt wat naby die rand van die prentjie wegkruip, is maklik om mis te kyk, en dit verander die antwoord.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en:
The sketch shows the graphs of  f(x) = cos x  and  g(x) = cos 2x  for  x ∈ [−180° ; 180°].  A(120° ; −0,5) is one of the points where the graphs cut each other, and B is another.

Write down the coordinates of B.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af:
Die skets toon die grafieke van  f(x) = cos x  en  g(x) = cos 2x  vir  x ∈ [−180° ; 180°].  A(120° ; −0,5) is een van die punte waar die grafieke mekaar sny, en B is nog een.

Skryf die koördinate van B neer.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Both of these graphs are mirror images of themselves in the y-axis. So if they cut each other at 120°, where else must they cut each other?
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Albei hierdie grafieke is hul eie gereflekteerde beeld in die y-as. As hulle mekaar by 120° sny, waar anders moet hulle mekaar sny?

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Both f and g are cosine graphs, and every cosine graph is symmetrical about the y-axis.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: f en g is albei cos-grafieke, en elke cos-grafiek is simmetries om die y-as.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: So B is the mirror image of A:  B(−120° ; −0,5)
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Dus is B die gereflekteerde beeld van A:  B(−120° ; −0,5)

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: WATCH OUT: only the x-coordinate changes sign. The mirror is the y-AXIS, so a point reflects sideways and keeps its height. Writing B(−120° ; 0,5) flips the wrong coordinate.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: PASOP: net die x-koördinaat verander van teken. Die refleksie is in die y-AS, so 'n punt beweeg links of regs en behou sy hoogte. As jy B(−120° ; 0,5) skryf, draai jy die teken van die verkeerde koördinaat om.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Symmetry is the fastest tool on a graph-reading question, and here both curves have the same one: a cosine graph always looks the same on the left of the y-axis as it does on the right. If you folded the page along the y-axis, f would land on itself and so would g. That means every crossing point also lands on another crossing point. A is 120° to the right of the fold, so its partner is 120° to the left, at −120°. The height does not change, because folding sideways does not move anything up or down, so B keeps A's y-value of −0,5. Say the reason out loud when you write it: the mark is for knowing WHY, not just for the coordinates.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Simmetrie is die vinnigste hulpmiddel by 'n grafiekleesvraag, en hier het albei kurwes dieselfde simmetrie: 'n cos-grafiek lyk altyd links van die y-as dieselfde as regs daarvan. As jy die bladsy langs die y-as vou, sal f op homself val en g ook. Dit beteken elke snypunt val ook op 'n ander snypunt. A is 120° regs van die vou, so sy maat is 120° links daarvan, by −120°. Die hoogte verander nie, want 'n vou om die y-as skuif niks op of af nie, so B behou A se y-waarde van −0,5. Sê die rede hardop as jy dit skryf: die punt is daarvoor dat jy weet WAAROM, nie net vir die koördinate nie.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Write down the values of x for which  f(x) = g(x)  in the given interval.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Skryf die waardes van x neer waarvoor  f(x) = g(x)  in die gegewe interval.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: You already have two of them. Look carefully at the y-axis — do the two graphs meet there as well?
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Jy het reeds twee daarvan. Kyk mooi na die y-as: ontmoet die twee grafieke mekaar daar ook?

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: The curves meet at A, at B, and once more on the y-axis, where both graphs are at their maximum of 1.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Die kurwes ontmoet mekaar by A, by B, en nog een keer op die y-as, waar albei grafieke by hul maksimum van 1 is.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: x = −120°,  x = 0°  and  x = 120°
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: x = −120°,  x = 0°  en  x = 120°

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: The crossing on the y-axis is the one people miss, because it does not look like a crossing — the two curves touch there and separate again rather than passing through each other. It counts all the same. Both f and g are at their highest point when x is zero: cos 0° is 1 and cos 0° is also 1, so both graphs are at a height of 1 at the same moment, which is exactly what f(x) = g(x) means. The lesson is to read a graph for equal heights rather than for dramatic crossings. Anywhere the two curves touch, meet or cross, they are equal there.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Die snypunt op die y-as is die een wat mense mis, want dit lyk nie soos 'n snypunt nie: die twee kurwes raak mekaar daar en skei weer, eerder as om deur mekaar te gaan. Dit tel nogtans. f en g is albei by hul hoogste punt wanneer x nul is: cos 0° is 1 en cos 0° is ook 1, so albei grafieke is op dieselfde oomblik op 'n hoogte van 1, en dit is presies wat f(x) = g(x) beteken. Die les is om 'n grafiek vir gelyke hoogtes te lees eerder as vir dramatiese snypunte. Oral waar die twee kurwes raak, ontmoet of sny, is hulle daar gelyk.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: For which values of x is  f(x) ≥ g(x)?
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Vir watter waardes van x is  f(x) ≥ g(x)?

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Draw a light vertical cut line through every point where the graphs meet. Then look at each strip in turn and ask one question: which curve is on top here?
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Teken 'n ligte vertikale snylyn deur elke punt waar die grafieke ontmoet. Kyk dan na elke interval op sy beurt en vra een vraag: watter kurwe is hier bo?

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Cut the interval at the meeting points:  x = −120°, 0° and 120°.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Sny die interval by die ontmoetingspunte:  x = −120°, 0° en 120°.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: In the strips between −120° and 120° the f curve is on top (or level with g at the meeting points). Outside them, g is on top.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: In die intervalle tussen −120° en 120° is die f-kurwe bo (of gelyk met g by die ontmoetingspunte). Buite hulle is g bo.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: REMEMBER: the sign is ≥, not >, so the meeting points themselves are INCLUDED — at −120° and 120° the two graphs are equal, which still satisfies \"f is greater than or equal to g\". Use ≤ signs in your answer, not < signs.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: ONTHOU: die teken is ≥ en nie > nie, so die ontmoetingspunte self is INGESLUIT: by −120° en 120° is die twee grafieke gelyk, wat steeds aan \"f is groter as of gelyk aan g\" voldoen. Gebruik ≤-tekens in jou antwoord, nie <-tekens nie.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: This is her cut-line-and-paint method, and it works on trig graphs exactly as it does on parabolas. First find every place the two graphs meet, and rule a light vertical line through each one — those are the only places where the answer can change from true to false. Here that gives cut lines at −120°, 0° and 120°, which chop the interval into four strips. Then walk the strips one at a time and ask which curve is higher. Nothing has to be calculated; you are reading. Between −120° and 120°, f sits at or above g the whole way, including at the touching point on the y-axis, so those two strips join into one answer. Outside them g is higher. Last, match your brackets to the sign in the question.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Dit is haar snylyn-en-verf-metode, en dit werk op trig-grafieke presies soos op parabole. Kry eers elke plek waar die twee grafieke ontmoet, en teken 'n ligte vertikale lyn deur elkeen: dit is die enigste plekke waar die antwoord van waar na onwaar kan verander. Hier gee dit snylyne by −120°, 0° en 120°, wat die interval in vier intervalle opkap. Gaan dan die intervalle een vir een deur en vra watter kurwe hoër is. Niks hoef bereken te word nie; jy lees. Tussen −120° en 120° lê f die hele pad op of bo g, ook by die raakpunt op die y-as, so daardie twee intervalle word een antwoord. Buite hulle is g hoër. Laastens: pas jou hakies by die teken in die vraag aan.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en:
The sketch shows the graphs of  f(x) = cos x  and  g(x) = sin x  for  x ∈ [0° ; 360°].

Write down the coordinates of the x-intercepts of f in the given interval.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af:
Die skets toon die grafieke van  f(x) = cos x  en  g(x) = sin x  vir  x ∈ [0° ; 360°].

Skryf die koördinate van die x-afsnitte van f in die gegewe interval neer.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: An x-intercept is where the graph is at height zero. Read them straight off the sketch — a cosine crosses the axis a quarter of a period in, and every half period after that.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: 'n x-afsnit is waar die grafiek op hoogte nul is. Lees hulle reguit van die skets af: 'n cos-grafiek sny die as 'n kwart periode in, en daarna elke halwe periode.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: cos x = 0  at a quarter of a period and again three quarters of the way through.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: cos x = 0  by 'n kwart periode en weer driekwart van die pad deur.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Finding where each graph crosses the x-axis is the setting-up step for every product question, so it is worth doing carefully even when it looks trivial. A cosine starts at its maximum and first reaches zero a quarter of a period later, which here is 90°. After that it crosses every half period, so the next one is at 270°. The question asked for coordinates, not just x-values, so write them as ordered pairs with the zero included. It is also worth noting g's intercepts while you are here — sin x is zero at 0°, 180° and 360° — because part (b) needs both lists.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Om te kry waar elke grafiek die x-as sny, is die opstelstap vir elke produkvraag, so dit is die moeite werd om dit versigtig te doen, selfs as dit triviaal lyk. Die cos-grafiek begin by sy maksimum en bereik nul vir die eerste keer 'n kwart periode later, wat hier 90° is. Daarna sny dit elke halwe periode, so die volgende een is by 270°. Die vraag het koördinate gevra, nie net x-waardes nie, so skryf hulle as geordende pare met die nul ingesluit. Let sommer ook nou op g se afsnitte (sin x is nul by 0°, 180° en 360°), want deel (b) het albei lyste nodig.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: For which values of x is  f(x)·g(x) < 0?
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Vir watter waardes van x is  f(x)·g(x) < 0?

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: A product is negative when the two things being multiplied have OPPOSITE signs. So look for the stretches where one curve is above the x-axis while the other is below it.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: 'n Produk is negatief wanneer die twee dinge wat vermenigvuldig word TEENOORGESTELDE tekens het. Soek dus die stukke waar een kurwe bo die x-as is terwyl die ander onder dit is.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: A product is negative when one factor is positive and the other is negative — so look for where one curve is ABOVE the x-axis and the other is BELOW it.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: 'n Produk is negatief wanneer een faktor positief en die ander negatief is: soek dus waar een kurwe BO die x-as is en die ander ONDER dit.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Cut the interval at every x-intercept of either graph:  x = 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°, 360°.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Sny die interval by elke x-afsnit van enige van die grafieke:  x = 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°, 360°.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en:
90° to 180°:  g is above, f is below  ⟹  product negative ✔
270° to 360°:  f is above, g is below  ⟹  product negative ✔
the other two strips have both curves on the same side ⟹ product positive
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af:
90° tot 180°:  g is bo, f is onder  ⟹  produk negatief ✔
270° tot 360°:  f is bo, g is onder  ⟹  produk negatief ✔
in die ander twee intervalle is albei kurwes aan dieselfde kant ⟹ produk positief

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: 90° < x < 180°   or   270° < x < 360°
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: 90° < x < 180°   of   270° < x < 360°

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: WATCH OUT: the sign is <, so the ends are NOT included. At x = 90°, 180° and 270° one of the graphs is exactly zero, which makes the product zero — and zero is not less than zero. Use round brackets or strict inequality signs.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: PASOP: die teken is <, so die eindpunte is NIE ingesluit nie. By x = 90°, 180° en 270° is een van die grafieke presies nul, wat die produk nul maak, en nul is nie kleiner as nul nie. Gebruik ronde hakies of streng ongelykheidstekens.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: A product question is a signs question, so stop thinking about heights and think only about above or below. The rule is the one you already know from multiplying numbers: two positives give a positive, two negatives give a positive, and one of each gives a negative. So you are hunting for the stretches where one curve is above the axis while the other is below it. The setting up is what makes it manageable. Rule a cut line at every x-intercept of EITHER graph, because those are the only places a sign can change, and then walk the strips one at a time writing a plus or a minus for each curve. Multiply the two signs in each strip and collect the strips that came out negative. Finally check the ends: where either graph is zero the product is zero, so a strict inequality leaves those points out.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: 'n Produkvraag is 'n tekensvraag, so hou op om aan hoogtes te dink en dink net aan bo of onder. Die reël is die een wat jy reeds ken van getalle vermenigvuldig: twee positiewes gee 'n positief, twee negatiewes gee 'n positief, en een van elk gee 'n negatief. Jy soek dus die stukke waar een kurwe bo die as is terwyl die ander onder dit is. Die opstelwerk maak dit hanteerbaar. Teken 'n snylyn by elke x-afsnit van ENIGE van die grafieke, want dit is die enigste plekke waar 'n teken kan verander, en gaan dan die intervalle een vir een deur en skryf 'n plus of 'n minus vir elke kurwe. Vermenigvuldig die twee tekens in elke interval en versamel die intervalle wat negatief uitkom. Kontroleer laastens die eindpunte: waar enige van die grafieke nul is, is die produk nul, so 'n streng ongelykheid laat daardie punte uit.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en:
The sketch shows the graphs of  f(x) = sin x  and  g(x) = sin 2x  for  x ∈ [−90° ; 180°].  The dots mark three of the points where the graphs meet; they also meet at  x = 180°.

Write down the period of g.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af:
Die skets toon die grafieke van  f(x) = sin x  en  g(x) = sin 2x  vir  x ∈ [−90° ; 180°].  Die kolletjies wys drie van die punte waar die grafieke ontmoet; hulle ontmoet ook by  x = 180°.

Skryf die periode van g neer.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: The 2 is with the x, so it squashes the graph. Divide 360° by it.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Die 2 is by die x, so dit druk die grafiek saam. Deel 360° daardeur.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Period of g = 360° ÷ 2
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Periode van g = 360° ÷ 2

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: period of g = 180°
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: periode van g = 180°

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Note that this part is about g, the squashed one, not about f. Its b is 2, so its period is 180° — half of f's. On the sketch that shows up as g completing a whole wave in the space f only gets halfway through, which is what makes the two curves cross each other several times instead of once or twice. Working out both periods before you start an inequality question is worth the ten seconds: the ratio between them tells you roughly how many crossings to expect, so you know whether you have found them all.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Let op dat hierdie deel oor g gaan, die saamgedrukte een, nie oor f nie. Sy b is 2, so sy periode is 180°: die helfte van f s'n. Op die skets wys dit as g wat 'n hele golf voltooi in die ruimte waar f net halfpad kom, en dit is waarom die twee kurwes mekaar 'n paar keer sny in plaas van een of twee keer. Om albei periodes uit te werk voordat jy 'n ongelykheidsvraag begin, is die tien sekondes werd: die verhouding tussen hulle sê vir jou rofweg hoeveel snypunte om te verwag, so jy weet of jy hulle almal gekry het.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Cut the picture at every point where the graphs meet — there are four of them in this interval — and then walk the strips asking which curve is on top.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Sny die prentjie by elke punt waar die grafieke ontmoet (daar is vier in hierdie interval) en gaan dan die intervalle deur en vra watter kurwe bo is.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Cut lines at every meeting point:  x = −60°, 0°, 60° and 180°.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Snylyne by elke ontmoetingspunt:  x = −60°, 0°, 60° en 180°.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en:
−90° to −60°: g on top ✘   |   −60° to 0°: f on top ✔
0° to 60°: g on top ✘   |   60° to 180°: f on top ✔
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af:
−90° tot −60°: g bo ✘   |   −60° tot 0°: f bo ✔
0° tot 60°: g bo ✘   |   60° tot 180°: f bo ✔

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: −60° ≤ x ≤ 0°   or   60° ≤ x ≤ 180°
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: −60° ≤ x ≤ 0°   of   60° ≤ x ≤ 180°

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: WATCH OUT: two separate strips means two separate pieces in your answer, joined by the word OR. Writing −60° ≤ x ≤ 180° would claim the middle strip as well, where g is actually the higher graph.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: PASOP: twee aparte intervalle beteken twee aparte stukke in jou antwoord, verbind deur die woord OF. As jy −60° ≤ x ≤ 180° skryf, eis jy ook die middelste interval op, waar g eintlik die hoër grafiek is.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: The more often two graphs cross, the more the cut-line habit earns its keep. Start by marking every place the curves meet, because between two meetings the same curve stays on top the whole way — it cannot overtake without crossing. Here there are four meetings, which cut the interval into four strips, and you only need to check one point in each strip to know which curve wins there. Then collect the winning strips. Two of them are not next to each other, so the answer has two separate pieces and needs the word or between them, not a single long inequality. Last, look at the sign in the question: it is greater-than-or-equal, so the meeting points themselves belong in the answer and the brackets are the closed kind.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Hoe meer twee grafieke mekaar sny, hoe meer betaal die snylyn-gewoonte. Begin deur elke plek te merk waar die kurwes ontmoet, want tussen twee ontmoetings bly dieselfde kurwe die hele pad bo: dit kan nie verbygaan sonder om te sny nie. Hier is daar vier ontmoetings, wat die interval in vier intervalle opkap, en jy hoef net een punt in elke interval te toets om te weet watter kurwe daar wen. Versamel dan die wen-intervalle. Twee daarvan lê nie langs mekaar nie, so die antwoord het twee aparte stukke en het die woord of tussen hulle nodig, nie een lang ongelykheid nie. Kyk laastens na die teken in die vraag: dit is groter-as-of-gelyk-aan, so die ontmoetingspunte self hoort in die antwoord en die hakies is die geslote soort.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en:
The sketch shows the graphs of  f(x) = sin x  and  g(x) = cos 2x  for  x ∈ [0° ; 360°].

For which values of x is f increasing?
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af:
Die skets toon die grafieke van  f(x) = sin x  en  g(x) = cos 2x  vir  x ∈ [0° ; 360°].

Vir watter waardes van x is f stygend?

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: \"Increasing\" means the curve is going UP as you read from left to right. Trace f with your finger and mark where it climbs.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: \"Stygend\" beteken die kurwe gaan OP as jy van links na regs lees. Volg f met jou vinger en merk waar dit klim.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: f climbs from the origin up to its maximum, then falls to its minimum, then climbs again to the end of the interval.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: f klim van die oorsprong op tot by sy maksimum, val dan tot by sy minimum, en klim dan weer tot aan die einde van die interval.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: 0° < x < 90°   or   270° < x < 360°
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: 0° < x < 90°   of   270° < x < 360°

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Increasing and decreasing are read left to right, exactly like reading a sentence. Put your finger at the left-hand end of the graph and drag it along the curve: wherever your finger rises, the graph is increasing, and wherever it drops, the graph is decreasing. The change always happens at a turning point, which is why turning points are the natural cut lines for this kind of question. Here f rises out of the origin to its maximum at 90°, then falls all the way to its minimum at 270°, then rises again to the end. So there are two separate rising stretches. Turning points themselves are neither rising nor falling, which is why the ends are left out with strict inequality signs.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Stygend en dalend word van links na regs gelees, net soos jy 'n sin lees. Sit jou vinger by die linkerkant van die grafiek en skuif dit langs die kurwe: oral waar jou vinger styg, is die grafiek stygend, en oral waar dit daal, is die grafiek dalend. Die verandering gebeur altyd by 'n draaipunt, en daarom is draaipunte die natuurlike snylyne vir hierdie soort vraag. Hier styg f uit die oorsprong tot by sy maksimum by 90°, val dan die hele pad tot by sy minimum by 270°, en styg dan weer tot aan die einde. Daar is dus twee aparte stygende stukke. Draaipunte self is nie stygend of dalend nie, en daarom word die eindpunte met streng ongelykheidstekens uitgelaat.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: For which values of x is g decreasing?
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Vir watter waardes van x is g dalend?

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: g completes two whole waves in this interval, so it falls twice. Find its turning points first — they are the places where falling turns into rising.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: g voltooi twee hele golwe in hierdie interval, so dit val twee keer. Kry eers sy draaipunte: dit is die plekke waar dalend oorgaan in stygend.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: g has period 360° ÷ 2 = 180°, so it makes two complete waves. Its turning points are at  x = 0°, 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: g het periode 360° ÷ 2 = 180°, so dit maak twee volledige golwe. Sy draaipunte is by  x = 0°, 90°, 180°, 270° en 360°.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: It falls from each maximum to the next minimum.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Dit val van elke maksimum tot by die volgende minimum.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: 0° < x < 90°   or   180° < x < 270°
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: 0° < x < 90°   of   180° < x < 270°

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: The squashed graph is the one that catches people out, because it turns twice as often as they expect. Work out its period first: 180°, so it fits two whole waves into the interval and therefore has twice as many turning points as f does. A cosine starts at a maximum, so g starts high, falls to a minimum at 90°, rises back to a maximum at 180°, falls again to a minimum at 270°, and finishes back at the top. The falling stretches are therefore from 0° to 90° and from 180° to 270°. Reading it off the picture is fine, but knowing the period first tells you how many falling stretches to expect, so you know when to stop looking.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Die saamgedrukte grafiek is die een wat mense vang, want dit draai twee keer so gereeld as wat hulle verwag. Werk eers sy periode uit: 180°, so dit pas twee hele golwe in die interval en het dus twee keer soveel draaipunte as f. Die cos-grafiek begin by 'n maksimum, so g begin hoog, val tot by 'n minimum by 90°, styg terug na 'n maksimum by 180°, val weer tot by 'n minimum by 270°, en eindig weer bo. Die dalende stukke is dus van 0° tot 90° en van 180° tot 270°. Om dit van die prentjie af te lees is goed, maar as jy eers die periode ken, weet jy hoeveel dalende stukke om te verwag, so jy weet wanneer om op te hou soek.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: Hence write down the values of x for which f is increasing while g is decreasing.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Skryf gevolglik die waardes van x neer waarvoor f stygend is terwyl g dalend is.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: You want the x-values that appear in BOTH of your previous answers. Sketch the two answers as strips on a number line and look for the overlap.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Jy soek die x-waardes wat in ALBEI jou vorige antwoorde voorkom. Skets die twee antwoorde as intervalle op 'n getallelyn en soek die oorvleueling.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en:
f increasing:  0° < x < 90°  or  270° < x < 360°
g decreasing:  0° < x < 90°  or  180° < x < 270°
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af:
f stygend:  0° < x < 90°  of  270° < x < 360°
g dalend:  0° < x < 90°  of  180° < x < 270°

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: The only stretch that appears in both lists:  0° < x < 90°
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Die enigste stuk wat in albei lyste voorkom:  0° < x < 90°

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: REMEMBER: the word \"while\" means BOTH things are happening at once, so you want the OVERLAP of your two answers, not both of them put together. Adding the strips up instead of overlapping them is the standard mistake here.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: ONTHOU: die woord \"terwyl\" beteken ALBEI dinge gebeur tegelyk, so jy soek die OORVLEUELING van jou twee antwoorde, nie albei saamgegooi nie. Om die intervalle bymekaar te tel in plaas van te oorvleuel, is die standaardfout hier.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: The word while is doing all the work in this question. It means both conditions have to be true at the same x, so you want the part the two answers share, not everything they cover between them. The safest way to find it is to draw a short number line from 0° to 360°, mark your f answer above the line and your g answer below it, and look for where the two markings sit over each other. Here f rises on two stretches and g falls on two stretches, and only one stretch is common to both, from 0° to 90°. This overlap-versus-add distinction comes up in every subject that uses intervals, and getting into the number-line habit now saves marks later in inequalities and in domain questions.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Die woord terwyl doen al die werk in hierdie vraag. Dit beteken albei voorwaardes moet by dieselfde x waar wees, so jy soek die stuk wat die twee antwoorde gemeen het, nie alles wat hulle saam dek nie. Die veiligste manier om dit te kry, is om 'n kort getallelyn van 0° tot 360° te teken, jou f-antwoord bo die lyn en jou g-antwoord onder die lyn te merk, en te kyk waar die twee merke oor mekaar lê. Hier styg f op twee stukke en val g op twee stukke, en net een stuk is gemeen aan albei, van 0° tot 90°. Hierdie verskil tussen oorvleuel en bymekaartel kom voor in elke vak wat intervalle gebruik, en as jy nou die getallelyn-gewoonte aanleer, spaar dit later punte by ongelykhede en by vrae oor die definisieversameling.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en:
The sketch shows the graphs of  f(x) = sin x  and  g(x) = cos x  for  x ∈ [0° ; 360°].  The graphs cut each other at A(45° ; 0,71) and at B.

Determine the coordinates of B.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af:
Die skets toon die grafieke van  f(x) = sin x  en  g(x) = cos x  vir  x ∈ [0° ; 360°].  Die grafieke sny mekaar by A(45° ; 0,71) en by B.

Bepaal die koördinate van B.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: The graphs are equal where  sin x = cos x,  which is where  tan x = 1.  That happens once every 180°, so B is half a turn along from A.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Die grafieke is gelyk waar  sin x = cos x,  dit is waar  tan x = 1.  Dit gebeur een keer elke 180°, so B is 'n halwe draai verder as A.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: sin x = cos x  ⟹  tan x = 1,  which repeats every 180°:  x = 45° + 180° = 225°
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: sin x = cos x  ⟹  tan x = 1,  wat elke 180° herhaal:  x = 45° + 180° = 225°

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: REMEMBER: B is NOT the mirror image of A in the y-axis. A sine graph and a cosine graph are not symmetrical about the y-axis in the same way, so the mirror trick that works on two cosines does not work here. Use the tangent repeat of 180° instead — or just read the second crossing off the sketch.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: ONTHOU: B is NIE die gereflekteerde beeld van A in die y-as nie. Die sin-grafiek en die cos-grafiek is nie op dieselfde manier simmetries om die y-as nie, so die refleksie-truuk wat by twee cos-grafieke werk, werk nie hier nie. Gebruik eerder die tan-herhaling van 180°, of lees net die tweede snypunt van die skets af.

tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.en: The two curves are equal where their heights match, so start from sin x = cos x. Dividing both sides by cos x turns that into tan x = 1, and a tangent repeats itself every 180°. So once you know one solution at 45°, the next is 180° later at 225°, and that is B's x-coordinate. For the height, put 225° back into either graph — both must give the same answer, which is a free check — and sin 225° is −0,71 to two decimal places. Reading it off the sketch is also allowed and gives the same answer: the second crossing is clearly down in the negative part of the picture, roughly two-thirds of a unit below the axis.
tgraph-siblings-intersections-inequaliti.af: Die twee kurwes is gelyk waar hul hoogtes ooreenstem, so begin by sin x = cos x.
